data.title: Pixel text review fixes: hardware-problem lines, conversion limits, error wording, .PIXELS case, one frame_size, schema help
data.description:
Why: review-pix15 (fifteenth session) of f6b8a97 (pixel text). Core promises hold (fuzzing, round trips, build equivalence incl. dmg N / PALETTE N, additive wire). These are the low findings, one unit of work.

Probes (red tests for this leaf) are in the kept worktree /Users/ben/git/gbcli/.claude/worktrees/agent-a83b54f36b35f685f: crates/pixels/tests/it/probe_review_pix15.rs (13 tests, 5 red: items 2,3,4,5,9) and crates/build/tests/it/probe_review_pix15.rs (5 tests, 3 red: items 1,6,7), each registered by one mod line in tests/it/main.rs. Not rustfmt-clean. Keep the green ones (fuzz, malformed input, positions, round trips, dmg N / palette build equivalence) as tests. Remove the worktree when this lands.

1. A hardware problem's line= names whoever drew the tile's top-left pixel (`locate`, crates/build/src/images/pipeline.rs), so a fill or earlier block wins over the block that drew the offending pixels. Probe ..._names_the_block_not_the_fill_under_the_tiles_corner: expected line=10, got 8.
2. from_raster (crates/pixels/src/png.rs) doesn't check MAX_SIDE (1024): a 1032x1 PNG converts to text the parser refuses. Refuse at conversion.
3. A color/fill/size line inside an unended block is told it "starts a block" (Parser::unended, text/parse/blocks.rs).
4. An empty indented block's error is at column 1, not at its header word (close() in blocks.rs).
5. frame_size("hero.16x16.dmg.pixels") is None (crates/pixels/src/name.rs); crates/build/src/images/find.rs has a private copy. One frame_size, owned in one place.
6. .PIXELS (upper case) is silently skipped while .PNG is found in any case: find.rs, two_forms, dmg_path, protocol palettes/rules.rs is_image_path.
7. An orphan town.dmg.pixels names only town.png as the missing color image; frame-size and image-name remedies in find.rs suggest .png for a .pixels file. Name the form the user is using, or both.
8. Docs: help/schema.rs:132 says assignment IMAGE is NAME.png (.pixels accepted too); the limit list (~125) lacks pixels_text; ImageProblem.column undescribed.
9. (suspected) help pixels and the design say --tiles keys read as the image's own tile numbers, but keys are per legend symbol while the build merges colors equal in RGB555 (#ffffff vs #fefefe: 2 vs 1). Fix the code to merge like the build if that's clean, else make the claim honest; say which.
Small, unprobed: with several outputs an I/O failure on the second leaves the first written (vs "nothing is written"); a bad palette file returns before pixels_text problems are added, hiding them.

data.title: Design pixel fonts, variable width, after GB Studio's atlas (decision for Ben)
data.description:
Why: Ben (2026-11-09) asked whether gbcli has a design for pixel fonts, and pointed at GB Studio's font atlas, whose variable-width fonts are desirable. Today a font is only a tileset (assets/tiles/font.png or .pixels): fixed 8x8 glyphs, one per tile, the program bringing its own CHARMAP (the racer wrote one by hand). Nothing in project/ or backlog.md covers variable width.

What: research, then a design doc for Ben (project/2026-11-09-pixel-fonts-design.md or later date), in the shape of the pixel text design: how GB Studio defines a font (its atlas image layout, how character widths are found or declared, character set and mapping, any metadata file, DMG/GBC handling) and how its engine draws variable-width text at run time (rendering glyphs into tiles, VRAM budget, speed), with sources (GB Studio is MIT-licensed on GitHub; cite files and lines). Then options for gbcli: the asset format (a glyph sheet in assets/fonts/? widths measured from art vs declared; .pixels support), what build emits (glyph data, width table, a charmap in images.inc), and whether the starter from `gbcli new` ships a renderer routine (as it ships a music player), with recommendations. Ben decides.

Out of scope: building it. Originality: learn the technique; don't copy GB Studio's art, fonts or code.

Research done (GB Studio eb6aa8a7, gbvm bd6f41cc = its submodule pin). Font = 8x8-cell PNG atlas (128x112 = 224 chars from code 32), width measured per cell by trimming magenta columns (fontData.ts:84-92), identical glyphs deduped, recode table byte->glyph, optional JSON mapping/table. Engine (gbvm ui.c:227-275, ui_a.s:88-185) shifts each glyph into a 2-tile WRAM buffer and uploads one tile per char into a 52-tile ring at $CC-$FF of the window's tiles. Also found: gbcli tilesets dedupe tiles, so a font tileset with two identical glyphs shifts every later index (output.rs/run.rs) -- a fixed-width font needs cells kept, not deduped. Writing project/2026-11-09-pixel-fonts-design.md next.

data.title: build --gbc writes build/NAME.gbc by default
data.description:
Why: the rogue built --gbc over its plain build's build/rogue.gb and ran DMG sessions on the GBC ROM for 20 minutes (project/2026-11-09-examples-dx-review-de.md item D-2). Ben, 2026-11-09: separate default names, with .gbc for the color build ("It already would have saved some time"). .gbc is the conventional extension for CGB-enhanced (dual, $80) and CGB-only ROMs; .gb for DMG.

What: a plain build writes build/NAME.gb as today; build --gbc defaults to build/NAME.gbc (its .sym and other sidecars beside it, named to match); --out still overrides. Every place that names the default (help, recipes, starter README or comments, rom_changed or session remedies, the examples' READMEs and scripts/examples/build-roms.sh where they rely on the default) follows. Un-parked from backlog.md ▸ Small run and view refinements.

criteria.label: build and build --gbc in one project leave both ROMs, NAME.gb and NAME.gbc, with matching .sym files
--out still wins, and every doc naming the default is updated

data.text: Ruling (Ben, 2026-11-09, relayed by the coordinator): option B. build --gbc defaults to build/gbc/NAME.gbc, with build/gbc/NAME.sym and build/gbc/NAME.map beside it; a plain build stays build/NAME.gb (+ build/NAME.sym, .map); --out still overrides either. Why a folder rather than build/NAME.gbc: every tool (rgblink's outputs, gbcli's session lookup in crates/bundle/src/session.rs and run/equiv.rs, SameBoy/BGB/Emulicious) finds a ROM's .sym by swapping its extension, so build/NAME.gb and build/NAME.gbc would share build/NAME.sym and the last build would silently give the other ROM wrong symbols. The extension-swap lookup is unchanged.

Built (build-de). Grammar (recorded in project/2026-11-06-design.md, "Update, 2026-11-09 (leaf IRgYTt): short blocks"): a `pattern` line names 1-4 columns, from channel 1. Each is Pn (shown here), - (none) or = (shown in another block); columns left off the end are =. A row has one cell per named column, and a cell under - or = must be blank. = adds nothing to the song (patterns are keyed by name), and the existing finish check still refuses an order whose pattern no block shows. Ambiguity: a short line could have meant "these patterns, any channel"; it is read positionally, as the four-column line is. to_text is unchanged. gbcli_music::EXAMPLE (help music's example and the starter's theme.song) now writes its second block as `pattern P4`. Tests: crates/music/tests/it/short_blocks.rs, which rewrites the example and all 15 hUGETracker samples with each shared pattern shown once and checks they give the same Song, the same canonical text and the same rgbds_asm. By hand: both example games' four songs, shortened, read back to their canonical text byte for byte.

Built (build-de). Starter: main.asm gains SECTION "Restart vectors", ROM0[$0000], `ds $40, $FF` (each byte rst $38). The red test showed it was needed in the starter itself: rgblink had floated the starter's own "Music" section to $0000 and a 1-byte test section to $003F. Test: build.rs the_starter_claims_the_restart_vectors_so_nothing_floats_into_them. palettes.txt cascade: pixel text that parses but names a palette entry that doesn't resolve is now its own Unread::Palette (build/src/images/pixels.rs). While palettes.txt failed to read, the pipeline drops those and keeps real pixel-text parse errors, so the existing test a_bad_palette_file_keeps_the_pixel_text_problems still holds. I chose this over parsing past the bad line: parse-past would still cascade when the bad line is itself a palette definition, and it would change parse()'s contract. Tests: images_pixels.rs a_bad_palette_file_is_the_only_error_its_palettes_references_get and a_palette_a_good_file_lacks_is_still_each_images_error.

Built (build-de). Verified on a starter ROM before writing: run --frames 3 stops at pc=$0040 VBlankVector ly=144 with wFrame=1, and one more frame shows wFrame=2, so the handler for the stop's VBlank runs in the next run. A starter patched to read the joypad into wJoy after each wake: run from frame 10 with --keys A@5 --until '[wJoy] != 0' first holds in frame 15, so K@N changes the buttons as frame N's VBlank begins and no earlier read sees it. Added: the frames-and-keys paragraph in help time; a pointer from run --help's --frames and --keys lines; "your script (not gbcli) logs each key change" in the bot recipe; u8/s8/u16/s16 in help expressions; i8[ / i16[ now give a syntax error with remedy "did you mean s8[ADDR]? ..." (engine cond/parse.rs, names::c_signed_width); help images: a 3-line which-kind lead and bg/town.png = forest and bg/town.pixels = forest on separate lines, with the palette_file remedy and the bad-line message showing both forms; help rgbds: the include/ line (checked with rgbasm 1.0.4: `ds N` of a symbol from another file gives "Expected constant expression: undefined symbol"). help.txt golden re-blessed.

Built (build-de). crates/build/src/project/layout.rs default_out: Dmg -> build/NAME.gb, Gbc -> build/gbc/NAME.gbc, so the .sym and .map follow by extension swap into build/gbc/. --out still wins. Tests: build.rs a_plain_and_a_gbc_build_leave_both_roms_with_their_own_sym_and_map (both ROMs survive, and the GBC .sym names ColorGbc while the plain one doesn't) and out_wins_over_the_gbc_default. Tests whose expectation changed with the ruling: build.rs the_gbc_target_writes_the_dual_mode_header... and gbcli_gbc_is_defined..., images_include.rs's .sym path, and the CLI's starter_gbc.rs, images_gbc.rs and rgbds.rs gbc paths; rgbds.txt golden re-blessed. Docs: help rgbds, help images (GBC lead and the both-machines example), build --help (--out and about), the starter README, racer/README.md and examples/README.md, docs/architecture.md, the design doc (marked update under the build --gbc bullet) and backlog.md. scripts/examples/build-roms.sh passes --out already, so it is unchanged, as are the rogue, rhythm and shooter READMEs. TDD lapse: I wrote the implementation before running the new tests red.

data.title: Pixel fonts: YAFF fonts, FontAsset, authoring, starter renderer
data.description: Why: Ben ruled the pixel fonts design on 2026-11-09, adopting LoadHigh asks 1-11 with five gbcli-side rulings (project/2026-11-09-pixel-fonts-design.md, "Ben's decisions"). Three leaves in order; LoadHigh can consume FontAsset after the first.

data.title: Fonts 1: strict YAFF, the font kind, build output, FontAsset, gbcli font
data.description: What (design ▸ Ben's decisions, ruling 4, first leaf): gbcli's own strict-subset YAFF reader and writer (no libyaff), tested against monobit's samples; assets/fonts/NAME.yaff as a kind (order kept, no dedupe, 1bpp, keys any UTF-8 character, u+XXXX or a name, NFC required for keys the mark table knows); build emits MainFontGlyphs, MainFontWidths and the charmap macro in images.inc/images.asm for fonts of at most 254 glyphs, and past that refuses with a remedy asking for a character list; FontAsset in gbcli_protocol in the assets op (glyph-number order; key, width, rows, drawn/composed; fixed), the op taking requested characters, uncapped; gbcli font FILE with --sample, --preview, --fit; gbcli help fonts stating the layout rules normatively.

criteria.label: a .yaff font builds to glyph and width tables and a charmap that assemble db strings to glyph numbers
the assets op returns a FontAsset for requested characters, with no cap
gbcli font --sample matches the layout rules in help fonts, and --fit fails past its width
a font past 254 glyphs is refused by build with a character-list remedy

data.title: Fonts 2: authoring: edit/save working copies, .chars, guides, BDF, new, diff, composition
data.description: What (design ▸ Ben's decisions, second leaf): gbcli font edit FONT.yaff --as png|bdf writes a gitignored working copy (PNG with a .chars sidecar, one line per row of cells, and guides as alpha 1-254) and prints its path; gbcli font save converts it back and removes it; build refuses while a copy is newer than its .yaff; every .chars/art disagreement is a problem naming the cell; gbcli font import FILE.bdf [--chars FILE] (trimmed glyphs placed by bounding box and ascent), export, new NAME --chars SET with guides and --guide-sheet, diff A B --png OUT; diacritics composed from gbcli's own mark table (Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A) for requested characters, a drawn glyph overriding, an overlap warning naming the glyph.

criteria.label: a font round-trips yaff to png+chars to yaff and yaff to bdf to yaff unchanged
a newer working copy blocks build, naming gbcli font save
a requested é is composed from e and U+0301 when not drawn, and reported as composed

data.title: Raycaster 1: prove a raycast view drawn into tile memory in gbcli
data.description:
Why: drawing a first-person view into VRAM fast enough to move through is the risky part; if the frame rate or the VRAM copy doesn't work, the game's shape changes (view size, frame rate, detail), so it goes first. Part of C, the raycaster in examples/raycaster/ (project/2026-11-09-raycaster-plan.md; the plan for all games is project/2026-11-08-example-games-plan.md).

What: `gbcli new` in examples/raycaster, then a fixed test map, a player position and angle, one ray per column with fixed-point DDA, wall heights from a distance table, walls drawn into a WRAM buffer laid out as the view's tiles, and the buffer copied into VRAM without writing in mode 3 (in VBlank, split over frames, or with the LCD briefly off; the agent's call, stated and shown). Turning and moving with the d-pad. A host reference renderer in examples/raycaster/tools/ with the ROM's own math and tables, compared with `gbcli shot` for several positions.

Already decided: users only (gbcli help, recipes, --help, README.md; never crates/, docs/, scripts/, project/ other than its own DX doc project/2026-11-09-dx-raycaster.md, or other examples). Build with `gbcli build` and `gbcli build --gbc` from this session on. The --gbc build may switch to double speed, but the DMG build must reach its own target without it (Ben, 2026-11-09). Write edit scripts to files, not inline `python3 -c`. Python 3 standard library only, for tools.

Open, the agent's call: view size (a smaller window than 160x144 is normal), columns per ray (1 or 2 pixels), flat or textured walls, the copy strategy. Name the game.

Risk: frame rate. Measure frames per view update with gbcli and state it; a first cut of a few updates a second is fine, ray2 optimizes.

no VRAM write lands in mode 3, shown by a gbcli command (gbcli help traps names one)
view updates per second stated, from the frame budget or measure, by a gbcli command shown
both builds succeed; the DX doc has this session's section

data.title: Raycaster 2: profile-driven optimization
data.description:
Why: this is the game's showcase: each speedup found by the profiler, measured before and after, and proven not to change the picture. Part of C (project/2026-11-09-raycaster-plan.md).

What: a fixed scripted walk (a keys file) and a baseline; then rounds of profile, change, measure, following `gbcli help optimize`: each round names the hot spot from --profile, the change, the cycles before and after by `gbcli measure` on a named span, and `gbcli equiv` against the baseline (or the reference tool, where a change is meant to alter pixels, such as a precision change). A table of the rounds goes in the DX doc. A `measure --max` assertion holds the final figure.

Already decided: as ray1. The agent stops when the view update hits its target or a round gains under 5%, and says which.

Open, the agent's call: the target update rate, which techniques to try (unrolled column fills, lookup tables in place of multiplies, fewer rays with doubled columns, partial-buffer copies).

data.title: Review fixes: font save over a newer font, overwriting exports, BDF overflow and round trip, Misaki help, U+FEFF
data.description:
Independent review (rev-fonts, eighteenth session) of 6feaf3e and c085c52; c085c52 and composition, protocol, version rule found sound. Probes (red): crates/font/tests/it/authoring_probes.rs, crates/build/tests/it/font_author_probes.rs on branch wt/rev-fonts.
1 HIGH: font save overwrites a .yaff edited after its working copy was made (font_save, crates/build/src/font_author/mod.rs:57-151, never compares; newer_copy at copies.rs:87 only guards the other direction). Fix: record the font's hash in the copy at edit; refuse at save if it changed, naming both files.
2 MEDIUM: export, new --guide-sheet and diff --png write over any path (write_files, io.rs:98), including the font itself or an unsaved working copy.
3 LOW: malformed BDF overflows (bdf/read.rs:227 ascent-(yo+h); xo+x; font_box ~141): panic in debug, misleading error in release. Checked arithmetic or bounds with the format remedy.
4 LOW: BDF round trip renames foo.bar to foo-bar and adds ascent/descent (bdf/write.rs:31, read.rs:263); the existing round-trip test hides it via Font::property's _/- equivalence.
5 LOW: font import help example claims Misaki's BDF imports directly (crates/cli/src/verbs/table_font.rs:151-152, help/schema.rs:243) but JISX0208 is refused.
7 LOW: U+FEFF as the first .chars cell is stripped as a BOM (chars.rs:29); escape it as <u+FEFF>.
6 (suspected, accepted debt): save's merge decision is interleaved with file I/O; recorded in project/2026-11-09-web-target.md by the main thread.

criteria.label: all eight rev-fonts probes pass, unchanged in intent
a save after the font changed is refused naming both files; a normal edit/save still works

data.title: Review fixes: text.asm's VBlank claim, the per-glyph bound (954, not 950), the test's pen offsets
data.description:
Independent review (rev-text, eighteenth session) of daf6d93: renderer sound at every pen offset and shade pair, LCD off for the starter's draw, DMG and GBC identical. Probe (green, coverage): crates/build/tests/it/rev_text_probe.rs on wt/rev-text.

2 MEDIUM: help fonts' bound 'at most 950 M-cycles a glyph' is exceeded: measured max 954 over every glyph at all 8 offsets (suspected: pen 7 plus .advance's page carry, +6). The test's two copies of the font sit 432 px apart (= 0 mod 8), so 94 of 95 glyphs run at one offset only, though the test and help claim two. Fix the test (offsets 0-7, crossing a page carry) and restate the bound.
3 LOW: TextLoadTiles' comment omits that a is 0 on return.

data.title: Review fixes: an RST entry keeps its slot name, the mark table's NFC claim, singletons in decomposed keys
data.description: rev-cli2's review of ae7261d (nineteenth session). F1 medium: names.rs:33-35 lets a label before an RST slot name the slot's entry byte, so a game labeling only Rst00 gets $0038 named Rst00+$38 (was RST_38); $0038 is where $FF execution lands. Fix: the slot name wins at the slot's first byte; the earlier label keeps the interior (Tetris $0031). The commit's test pins name(0x0038)=JumpTable+$10 though Tetris's table ends at $0033. data.description: A time-boxed spike: do SameBoy, the engine and the protocol handler build for wasm32 and run a ROM from JavaScript, and what would a web build of gbcli need? Ben chose it on 2026-11-09 as the next work after Stage 11. The plan, Ben's rulings (two agent sessions, Node plus a tiny page, installs allowed, new crates only on the spike/web branch, RGBDS research only) and what the findings decide: project/2026-11-09-web-spike-plan.md. data.title: Web spike 1: SameBoy, the engine and the handler built for wasm32, a ROM run from Node
data.description:
Why: the web ruling (AGENTS.md; project/2026-11-09-web-target.md) says nothing new may be designed that a web build couldn't use, but nobody has tried a web build. This session finds out whether the emulator half of gbcli builds and runs for wasm32, and what it costs. Session 1 of a two-session time box (Ben, 2026-11-09): stop at the end of the session with what you have and what blocked you.

What: on a branch spike/web, a spike crate (for example crates/web, a cdylib) that builds for wasm32 with SameBoy's C compiled for the same target, and exposes enough of the protocol handler to load a ROM (bytes, not a path), run N frames with keys, and return the frame and state as the protocol's own types (JSON across the JS boundary is fine). A Node script runs a committed test ROM (crates/sameboy/tests/roms/ or the starter's build) for a fixed number of frames and checks a frame hash against the native build's for the same ROM and inputs: exact equality, since runs are deterministic.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-09): agents may install the wasm32 Rust targets, a C sysroot (wasi-sdk or Emscripten) and wasm-bindgen-cli; new crates go only into the spike crate on spike/web, never main's workspace; spike code is disposable. Data, not paths, into core code; no new thread or clock in a core path (the web ruling).

Seams: crates/sameboy-sys (build.rs with the cc crate, the shim, the vendored patches), crates/engine (depends on gbcli-sameboy directly), crates/server (depends on gbcli-build for RGBDS subprocesses, gbcli-bundle for the filesystem and locks, a watchdog thread, Host::from_process). Expect to bypass or stub these in the spike crate, or put them behind cargo features on the branch; record each cut, since the list is the finding.

Open, the agent's call: which toolchain (wasi-sdk with wasm32-wasip1 and a WASI shim in Node, Emscripten with wasm32-unknown-emscripten, or wasm32-unknown-unknown with a minimal libc for SameBoy); try the one you judge likeliest first and say why. Out of scope: the browser page and timing (spike 2), RGBDS (its own leaf), any change landing on main.

Risks: SameBoy's C may use libc pieces with no wasm32 equivalent (file I/O for boot ROMs, setjmp, threads); the boot ROM is embedded or loaded, check which. The cc crate's wasm32 support depends on the sysroot. If the C won't build, that is a finding (it un-parks the bespoke-core backlog entry's web condition): record exactly what failed.

data.text:
Verified by probe (crates/gbcli/tests/cli/music.rs::the_wave_channel_sounds_an_octave_below_a_square_at_the_same_note): hUGEDriver's process_ch3 calls the same get_note_period/note_table as CH1/2, so A-3 is period 854 on both. The audio log names square 1 "A2 (109.78 Hz)" and the wave "A1 (54.89 Hz)" (gbcli_audio::pitch uses 131072 vs 65536 over 2048-period), and SameBoy's own per-channel WAVs measure ~110 Hz and ~55 Hz. So CH3 sounds one octave below the squares at the same note, the log already names the pitch heard (no fix needed), and the drum agent's "two octaves" = hUGETracker's +1 naming offset plus CH3's octave. help music now says so: on the wave channel C-3 sounds as C1 (33 Hz), two below its name; the log names it C1; write A-4 for an A2 bass.

Found on the way (not fixed, product behavior): a CH3 pattern whose cells equal a square channel's pattern is stored once, and the export counts instruments per pattern for the first channel whose orders name it (the deliberate hUGETracker port in gbcli_music::asm), so the wave instruments and waves are left out and hUGEDriver plays CH3 from garbage (random periods, NR51 toggling, level 0). My first probe song hit it. Candidate for a `gbcli song` warning or a help line.

data.title: Replace rgbgfx with a Rust encoder of gbcli's own image plan
data.description:
Why: nobody ships rgbgfx as wasm (project/2026-11-09-web-spike-rgbds.md), and a web build of gbcli needs image conversion without it. Ben asked (2026-11-09) what replacing it takes and asked for a leaf; the web track is paused, so this waits with it unless rgbgfx causes trouble on native.

What: gbcli already decides every pixel's color index (shade), packs GBC palettes and plans tiles and frame lists; it calls rgbgfx only with explicit palettes (-c), output (-o), the GBC attrmap (-a) and column-major sprites (-Z), never dedup or palette choice, then crates/build/src/images/agree.rs checks rgbgfx's tiles against the plan pixel by pixel. So the replacement is an encoder in Rust: 2bpp tile data and the attrmap from gbcli's own plan (crates/build/src/images/run.rs, gbc.rs), data in and data out per the web ruling. Turn agree.rs's comparison into a differential test against real rgbgfx over every image fixture and the example games, then drop rgbgfx from the build path (keep it as the test oracle, or retire it from doctor's toolchain checks: decide and say).

Estimate: about one agent session. Risks: rgbgfx edge cases gbcli doesn't yet pin (sprite transparency, GBC palette-slot choice where several palettes hold a tile's colors; agree.rs compares GBC by color for this reason).

data.title: Store parity through a blob, remove_tree of the root, and stopped_by asked before the flag is set (b9b50d7)
data.description:
Why: an independent verification of b9b50d7 (2026-11-10, verifier verify-hostfix) found all five review findings of Lr5CkM fixed and nothing major: no op reaches the disk or spawns a process on a denied host (every Op variant classified; 18 session and bundle ops probed over a real empty directory, with output paths aimed outside the project), and a caller's stop and the wall guard are told apart in every polling op. Four small things remain. None has a caller today; fix them together when the store or the interrupt is next touched, or narrow the docs.

1. MINOR. The trait doc (crates/bundle/src/project_store.rs, "The backings agree on the edge cases too") and docs/architecture.md's memory-backing bullet overstate parity. With `b` a blob: `put b/c`, `append b/c` and `make_dir b/c` answer NotADirectory on FileStore and NotFound on MemoryStore; `lock b/l` answers Io(NotADirectory) against Io(NotFound). Cause: State::writable answers not_found (crates/bundle/src/memory_store/state.rs:146-153) and insert_dir (state.rs:186). Callers that read NotFound as "missing" would misread a blob in the way on memory: checkpoints.rs:28/54, history.rs:34, store.rs:105, events.rs:124. Fix: memory answers NotADirectory when a parent is a blob (preferred), and add the four cases to store_parity_tests.rs.
2. NIT. remove_tree(Key::root()): FileStore deletes the project directory (kind None afterwards, a later put NotFound); MemoryStore keeps the root (kind Dir, put Ok), as project_store.rs's doc says both do.
3. NIT. Interrupt::stopped_by is documented as "asked once it is set" (crates/server/src/interrupt.rs:24) but is asked while the flag is clear: run/mod.rs:258 (probes.measure(..., self.interruption()) on every run), run/mod.rs:277 (the replay closure), run/measure.rs:42. Harmless for Watchdog and InterruptFlag, whose answer is fixed at arm; wrong for a third-party Interrupt that decides when asked. Fix: ask lazily, or reword the doc.
4. NIT. The Correction block added to project/2026-11-09-web-target.md sits inside a bullet list and splits it.

Reproductions: the verifier's probes were not kept (its worktree is removed). Each case above is one store call on each backing, or a scripted Interrupt that panics when asked with its flag clear.

data.title: Ask from ldh: return each named palette's DMG shade byte in the image results
data.description:
Why: an ask from LoadHigh (ldh), 2026-11-10; Ben ruled it (loadhigh project/2026-11-07-rulings-design-review.md ▸ Fortieth round 5; written up in loadhigh project/design/09-assets.md ▸ Palettes, Revision 17). In ldh a named palette on the DMG is a shade map: `bg.pal = NAME` loads one BGP byte, entry i's shade in bits 2i and 2i+1 (`palette inverted (black, darkgray, lightgray, white)` is $1B). Which shade a color gives is ruled to be gbcli's own shade rule (ShadeRule: the `dmg` line of assets/palettes.txt, or NamedPalettes.dmg from a client; each color takes its nearest entry's shade in RGB555), so the art and the palettes agree on one mapping and ldh never reimplements the rule.

What: return each named palette's DMG shade byte, computed by that rule, in the typed results of image conversion: a field beside ImagesMade.gbc.obj_palettes, or an emitted label per palette (ldh suggested `PaletteInvertedDmg`); gbcli chooses the form. ldh needs it per named palette, whether or not any image uses the palette.

Open for gbcli to decide: the form (field or label), and what a palette with two colors of one shade gives (ldh has no ruling; say what you return). This changes the protocol's result types, so it likely bumps PROTOCOL_VERSION (ldh pins 7 today); leave a note here with the commit and version so ldh can re-pin.

criteria.label: each named palette's DMG byte comes back in a typed result or an emitted label, by ShadeRule, with tests; the commit and protocol version are noted here for ldh

data.title: Ask from ldh: report the scroll (SCX, SCY) each line was drawn with in the raster report
data.description:
Why: an ask from LoadHigh (ldh), 2026-11-10 (loadhigh project/design/07-toolchain-cli.md, Revision 24; rulings ▸ Twenty-sixth round 2). ldh tests have `scroll_x_at(line)` and `scroll_y_at(line)`: the horizontal or vertical scroll a screen line is drawn with, so a raster effect is tested as `expect scroll_x_at(120) == ROAD[120]`. On the ROM, ldh derives it today from `run --raster`'s trace of writes to the scroll registers: a line's value is the last write that landed before that line's mode 3, or the value carried from the line before. That rule belongs to whoever knows the PPU, which is gbcli, and ldh restating it is a second copy that can drift.

What: have the raster report give, for each visible line (0 to 143), the SCX and SCY the line was drawn with (the latched values), beside the write trace it gives now. ldh will then read the value and drop its derivation.

Open for gbcli to decide: the shape (two arrays of 144, or one entry per line), whether window position and LCDC ride along, and what a mid-mode-3 write reports (ldh's tests do not need that case; say what you return). Likely a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump (ldh pins 7 today); leave a note here with the commit and version so ldh can re-pin.

criteria.label: the raster report gives each visible line's latched SCX and SCY, with tests; the commit and protocol version are noted here for ldh

data.label: each named palette's DMG byte comes back in a typed result or an emitted label, by ShadeRule, with tests; the commit and protocol version are noted here for ldh

data.note:
Done in dc3dad4, PROTOCOL_VERSION 8 (ldh can re-pin). Form: a typed field, ImagesMade.dmg_palettes: [{name, byte}], in the palettes' order, on every target (beside gbc, not in it, so a DMG build has it). byte is entry i's shade in bits 2i and 2i+1; 'inverted (black, darkgray, lightgray, white)' is $1B under a dmg line or grays.

Decided: two colors of one shade both write that shade (black, black, white, white is $0F), with no warning. A palette color no image has follows the project's rule: nearest entry under declared and known, clamped to the art's range under stretched, plain nearest with no art. An art color keeps the shade the art took. assets returns the bytes with no images at all; a build with no images still reports images: none (images_shade_edges pins that). Text output is unchanged: --json only.

data.label: the raster report gives each visible line's latched SCX and SCY, with tests; the commit and protocol version are noted here for ldh

data.note:
Done in dc3dad4, PROTOCOL_VERSION 8 (ldh can re-pin). Shape: RasterMade.drawn: [{frame, first_line, scx: [...], scy: [...]}], one entry per frame, entry i for line first_line + i, frame numbered as rows' frame. A whole frame is first_line 0 with 144 entries; a run starting or stopping mid-frame has fewer, so take a whole frame.

Each value is the register as that line's mode 3 began, sampled in the core at SameBoy's mode_3_start (patches/raster-line-scroll.patch), not derived from the write trace. A mid-mode-3 write is left out of that line's entry and first appears on the next line; it stays in rows with mode drawing. Window position and LCDC don't ride along. Text output is unchanged: --json only. The new patch changes the patch-set hash, so checkpoints from before it are refused as a mismatch.

data.text: Independent review of dc3dad4 (review-dc3dad4): no code bug. Correction to the note above for ldh: a write is left out of a line's entry only if it lands after that line's first tile fetch began (SameBoy's mode_3_start, 5 dots after STAT reads 3). A write in those 5 dots reports mode drawing but IS in the entry, and the line is drawn with it. Docs corrected and the LCD-on frame pinned by test in the following commit. Also: the frame after an LCD-on is listed in drawn although SameBoy publishes that frame blank, so align drawn.frame with pictures accordingly.

data.title: Stage 14: Teddy & Toys, an example game from Ben's design
data.description: A sixth example game, the first whose design is Ben's: a toy-factory arcade game from his sketch, built by an agent using gbcli as a user, and built to be tuned because Ben wants to iterate on the gameplay. The design, Ben's rulings and how the game agent works are in project/2026-11-16-teddy-and-toys-plan.md; the sketch is project/2026-11-16-teddy-and-toys-sketch.jpg. Read both before claiming a leaf.

data.title: Factory 1: prove the opposite belts, the still key column and the clock hand in gbcli
data.description:
Why: the scroll splits, the key column that must not scroll, and the clock hand are the game's technique and its screen's skeleton; if they don't hold, the layout changes, so they go first. Part of Teddy & Toys in examples/factory/ (project/2026-11-16-teddy-and-toys-plan.md, which holds Ben's full design).

What: `gbcli new` in examples/factory, then the screen from Ben's sketch with placeholder art. That means the HUD band at the top, the back (Finished) belt band at waist height and the front (parts) belt band at the bottom, scrolling in opposite directions at sub-pixel speeds by LY=LYC splits in HBlank. The key column on the right stays still over every line (the window layer is the natural tool; the agent proves its choice). An analog clock face has one hand that steps through pre-made rotations over a round, swapped into tile memory outside mode 3. The tuning file starts here (src/tuning.inc or similar), holding belt speeds, directions, the round length and the clock's step count, one commented constant each.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-16): the layout of the sketch; belts in opposite directions at constant speed; a single sweeping hand that turns red in the last 10 s on GBC; every gameplay number in one tuning file. Users only (gbcli help, recipes, --help, README.md, plus the plan doc, the sketch and its own DX doc project/2026-11-16-dx-factory.md; never crates/, docs/, scripts/, other examples or the rest of project/). Both builds from this session on. Writes to scroll registers stay in HBlank.

Open, the agent's call: band heights, how many clock rotations (60 one-second steps is the natural choice), how the clock tiles are laid out.

Risk: the window covers everything to its right and below WY, so the HUD and the key column share its constraints; say how the layout fits them.

criteria.label: raster evidence (gbcli run --raster --json, result.raster.drawn) shows each belt band's lines drawn with its own scroll and the key column's pixels unchanged across frames, by gbcli commands shown in the DX doc
shots a few seconds apart show both belts moved in opposite directions and the clock hand advanced, by gbcli commands shown
frame budget over a full round shows no lag frames, by a gbcli command shown
both builds succeed; the DX doc has this session's section

data.title: Factory 2: the shift, built to be tuned
data.description:
Why: turns the screen into the game Ben designed, in a shape he can iterate on. Part of Teddy & Toys (project/2026-11-16-teddy-and-toys-plan.md ▸ The design, and ▸ Built to be tuned).

What: the full one-minute round with placeholder art. The worker faces the parts belt (Down) or the Finished belt (Up). Pieces ride the parts belt with a skewed random supply. A grabs a piece in front of you if your hand is free and it matches the half you hold. B returns a half to the belt, where it keeps moving; with two halves it returns the last one grabbed. B+A together assembles, as a chord with a tunable window. B facing Finished with a whole toy drops it onto that belt and scores. Everything else buzzes. Held pieces show in the worker's hands. The score box counts toys, the clock ends the round, and a results screen shows the score and the personal best with "New best!", the best kept in battery-backed save RAM. The six toys and their halves are a data file turned into an include by a tool in tools/. Every gameplay number is in the tuning file. A rules check in tools/ runs one scripted scenario per rule in the plan's controls table and prints pass or fail per rule.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-16): the controls table in the plan exactly; no penalty for missed pieces; constant belt speed; no win or lose, just the score against a personal best. Users only, as factory1.

Open, the agent's call: the pick-up zone's width, the supply's skew rule, pieces as sprites or streamed background tiles (mind 10 sprites per line where the worker overlaps the back belt), the chord window's starting value.

Out of scope: final art and sound (factory3). Stop after this leaf: Ben playtests before art is made.

criteria.label: the rules check passes every rule in the controls table, and fails when a rule is broken on purpose (shown once in the DX doc)

a scripted bot plays a full round to the results screen with a nonzero score, and a second round shows the best score kept, also across a power cycle via gbcli sav or a restored save (commands in the DX doc)
every gameplay number is in the tuning file, and the toy include is generated from the toy data by a tool
no lag frames over the bot's round, by the frame budget
both builds succeed; the DX doc has this session's section

data.title: Factory 2b: playtest changes — one-piece slinky, Elle's turn step, bigger results text
data.description:
Why: Ben's playtest of the placeholder build (2026-11-16) asked for three gameplay changes, which land before the art so the art is drawn to the final behavior. Part of Teddy & Toys in examples/factory/ (project/2026-11-16-teddy-and-toys-plan.md ▸ Playtest rulings).

What:
- **The slinky's halves are one piece.** Any two slinky halves combine. In data/toys.txt (and so tools/gen_toys.py), a toy can declare that its two halves are the same piece. Holding one, the wanted piece is another of the same, and the supply's forced match follows that. Assembling two slinky halves makes the slinky.
- **Elle steps when she turns, and the turn costs time.** Facing the Finished belt, she stands about 8 px higher; facing the parts belt, lower. A side-view frame plays between the two, which can stay placeholder art here. The turn lasts TURN_FRAMES (a new constant in include/tuning.inc, starting at 8). During the turn A and B are ignored, with no buzz and no chord window started, and the new facing takes effect when the turn ends. Held pieces move with her hands.
- **Bigger text on the results screen:** the score, the best score and "New best!" at about twice the current height (a larger font or the current one drawn 2x; gbcli help fonts).

The rules check (tools/rules_check.py) grows a scenario for each: two slinky halves assemble; a slinky half refuses a different toy's half; A and B pressed during a turn do nothing and don't buzz; a press after TURN_FRAMES acts on the new facing.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-16): as above, and the plan's controls table otherwise unchanged. Ignoring presses during a turn (rather than buffering them) was the main thread's call; keep it a small change to flip. Users only, as the earlier leaves (gbcli help, recipes, --help, README.md, plus the plan, the sketch and the DX doc project/2026-11-16-dx-factory.md).

That review ranks what three game agents (and the integrator) stumbled on while building examples/teddy-and-toys with gbcli as users. data.title: A frame that turns the LCD off counts as lcd_off, not lag (F-1)
data.description:
Why: the frame budget calls the frame that starts a screen change a lag frame. Teddy & Toys' round end turns the LCD off early in frame 3666 (in VBlank) to draw the results screen; that frame reads lag true, lcd_off false, active_t 70204, while frames 3667-3672 read lcd_off. Every proof in the game had to name the frame as an exception. `gbcli help budgets` says "A frame the LCD was off for (startup, a screen change) counts as lcd_off, not lag", which a reader takes to include the frame that turns it off.

What: a frame in which the LCD was turned off, and which never halted while the LCD was on, counts as lcd_off. A frame with the LCD on throughout that never halted stays lag. Update `help budgets` to say exactly that.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-16, review question 1). Seams: the frame-budget classifier and its tests; `help budgets`; any golden that pins a frame-budget result. Reproduction: from examples/teddy-and-toys, `python3 tools/bot.py --gbcli <bin>`, then `gbcli run build/teddy-and-toys.gb --session lagprobe --from boot --frames 3700 --keys-file build/bot.keys --keys-since boot --frame-budget --json`.

Risk: callers that count lag may see a number change; say so in the commit message.

data.title: `shot` gives a pixel fingerprint and the screen as data, both honoring --crop (F-5)
data.description:
Why: comparing two shots meant decoding PNGs. Identical screens are different files, because shot writes the frame into tEXt chunks. Teddy & Toys' agent wrote a PNG decoder (tools/png.py), the second agent to do so, which met the un-park condition of the backlog entry "The screen's shade indices as data in shot --json" (now removed from backlog.md).

What: shot reports a fingerprint of the pixels (pixels= on its row and in --json), equal for equal pixels whatever the frame label. --json also carries the screen as data: shade indices (0-3) on a DMG and colors on a GBC, row by row. Both honor --crop, covering just the cropped region. The PNG keeps its tEXt chunks. shot --help documents the fingerprint (what it hashes) and the data's shape.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-16, review question 4: "both seem attractive ... especially if the agent can crop the raw data output window"). Seams: the shot path in the engine (the decision belongs in a library crate, per the web-target ruling), the protocol type for the shot result (one shared struct), the CLI row, shot --help, the schema. This applies to run --shot too, wherever a shot is taken.

Open, the builder's call: the hash function (stable across platforms and wasm32; no new dependency without asking), and whether the data is nested rows or a flat array with width and height.

data.title: Help and onboarding text where the Teddy & Toys agents looked (F-6, F-7, F-9 to F-13)
data.description:
Why: Ben's ruling: an agent's misreading of gbcli is a flaw in the help or onboarding text. Each item below cost an agent time because the text it read didn't say it, even where another topic did.

What, one change each:
- F-6: by `--wav --channels each` in run --help: every DAC switch pops at full scale whatever the volume, and each per-channel file opens with a step when its channel was already sounding as the run began, so peak levels mislead (use a windowed RMS past the opening).
- F-7: help images: each image's data sits in a ROMX section, so on an MBC cart switch to BANK(label) before reading it.
- F-9: run --help's --keys and --keys-file lines carry the one-sentence rule (K@N is seen by every joypad read after frame N's VBlank; a stop shows the frame just drawn) and point to `gbcli help time`; the bot recipe repeats it.
- F-10: help rgbds: rgbfix keeps a cartridge type written at $0147, and a battery save needs a type with a battery, such as $1B (MBC5+RAM+BATTERY).
- F-11: the `gbcli new` starter README's layout section and help rgbds: a project's own .inc files go in include/, the only folder INCLUDE searches.
- F-12: power-cycle's row and --help: the machine is at power-on and the boot ROM runs first, so run to the program's main loop (`run --to <label>`) before reading its state.
- F-13: every text view that truncates (the audio log's "more" row first) says how many rows are hidden and how to see them (--json, or --piano for audio).

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-16, review question 5). Seams: crates/cli help topics and verb help, the starter template's README, recipes; CLI goldens that pin help text. The help topic links checker (scripts/help/check-doc-links.py) if a link is added.

Out of scope: the per-channel loudness figure and filmstrip crop (leaf audio).

data.text:
Roster (2026-11-17, Ben chose all five in parallel):
- s15-budget: Dm8G8G (F-1 lcd_off), then UltxXY (F-2 build --out).
- s15-session: NQKwil (F-3/F-4).
- s15-shot: sL0Oa8 (F-5), plus the --filmstrip --crop half of YZth2Z (F-8), because it shares the crop path with shot. The integrator marks that YZth2Z criterion at merge.
- s15-audio: YZth2Z, loudness half only (F-6 per-channel windowed RMS).
- s15-help: rKKR0I (F-6 text, F-7, F-9..F-13).
run --help is touched by session, audio and help (separate lines); conflicts resolved at integration.

s15-audio (loudness half, F-6): built in worktree s15-audio. --audio-summary now carries summary.loudness[] (gbcli_audio::loudness): per take (mix first, then channels loudest first), the median of the 1/64 s (512-sample) windows' DC-removed RMS in dBFS, over windows above -72 dBFS, leaving out the capture's first window and every window within 128 samples of a DAC switch named by the write log (NRx2 bits 3-7, NR30 bit 7, NR52 power off). Takes come from the same muted replays as --channels each (shared, replayed once). SGB: no loudness, summary still counts writes. Criterion yzB passes by test on new ROM crates/audio/tests/roms/loudness.asm (seen failing first); its WAVs' plain RMS ranks the quiet channel louder, asserted in the test. eIu (crop/filmstrip) left for s15-shot.

s15-shot (branch wt/s15-shot), uncommitted, all suites green.

sL0Oa8 (F-5): ShotMade gains `pixels` (fingerprint) and `screen` {kind: shades|colors, width, height, rows}. Decided:
- Fingerprint: first 16 hex digits of SHA-256 (the workspace's own gbcli_engine::sha256, no new dependency) over the screen's rows joined by "\n". Reproducible in one line of Python from --json; the rows' count and length carry the size, so another crop shape can't share bytes. On a DMG it hashes shade indices (0-3 after BGP/OBPx), so equal pixels = equal shades.
- Data: rows as text, one per row (a digit per pixel for shades, rrggbb per pixel for colors), following the view verb's tiles/map rows precedent.
- "Colors on a GBC": the 24-bit color the core output and the PNG holds (SameBoy's conversion of RGB555), not palette RAM's RGB555, which the framebuffer doesn't keep.
- Decision lives in gbcli-view (screen.rs, Frame::cropped); server wires it.
Criteria: Bs7 by view unit tests (one-pixel change, shape change) + server shot_screen_tests (frames 3 vs 5 equal; BGP inverted differs). bfj by shot_screen_tests (DMG shades + crop narrows rows and fingerprint; GBC colors + crop). vOk: shot --help about, --crop/--shot flag lines, schema (result.shot shape, filmstrip args, SHOT scale fixed 1-8 -> 1-16).

YZth2Z filmstrip half (eIu, for the integrator to mark): FilmstripArgs.crop; run --crop accepted with --filmstrip, crops every frame (PNG labeled `crop x=.. y=.. w=.. h=..`). Tests: server filmstrip_tests::a_crop_applies_to_every_frame_of_the_strip (pixel-exact against an uncropped strip), cli flag_tests::run_crop_crops_the_filmstrip..., CLI golden filmstrip.txt.

Cost to flag: --json on a full-screen shot now carries ~24 KB (DMG) or ~140 KB (GBC) of rows; --crop narrows it.

Ruling (Ben, 2026-11-17): the screen data in shot --json is opt-in behind a flag; plain --json carries the pixels= fingerprint only. s15-shot measured a full screen at about 24 KB of rows on a DMG and 140 KB on a GBC, too much to arrive unasked in an agent's context.

Ruling (Ben, 2026-11-17): the leaf's premise was wrong. s15-budget found that Teddy & Toys' lag frame is the frame before the LCD turns off. The game runs di and polls LY for VBlank with the LCD on, and the LCD goes off just after the boundary. The classifier already counts a frame that turns the LCD off as lcd_off (test frames_with_the_lcd_off_are_marked_and_not_lag). Ben chose lookahead: a frame that never halted counts as lcd_off if the next frame turns the LCD off before it halts. A frame with the LCD on throughout that never halted, followed by a frame that does not turn the LCD off before halting, stays lag. Criterion (a) is reread to that rule; (b) lag 0 stands.

data.title: session_created skips to the second response when serve's first line doesn't parse (3c60aed)
data.description:
Found by review s15-r-engine of 3c60aed. Handler::handle attaches the report (crates/server/src/handle/mod.rs, `response.session_created = self.session_created.take()`), but serve::answer_line (crates/server/src/serve.rs:59-65) answers an unparseable or non-UTF-8 line without calling the handler, so the report rides on the second response. Same gap: a handler panic (catch_unwind builds the response, take() never reached); serve/batch with no request lines (never shown); batch rows mode prints session_created after `line n=1 ok=0`.
Reproduction: probe crates/server/src/handle/s15_probe_tests.rs::probe_session_created_rides_on_the_first_serve_response_even_a_bad_line (in the reviewer's worktree; the fixer gets it in the brief) fails with lines[0].session_created == None.
Suggested fix: take the report at the serve layer (an Answer::take_session_created() hook, default None, applied by serve() to whatever response it writes, parse/UTF-8 errors and panics included). Decide whether empty input still reports the creation.

criteria.label: the reviewer's probe passes: the first serve response carries session_created even for a bad line
a handler panic and batch rows mode report it first too, by test

data.title: Misplaced doc comments, run --help's last-frame clause, and the color note's remedy in the CLI (3c60aed, e3ff57c)
data.description:
Found by review s15-r-engine of 3c60aed and e3ff57c. Three text defects:
1. crates/cli/src/render/mod.rs:92-96: `pub fn session_created` sits between `rows`'s doc comment and `rows`, so it carries both and `rows` has none.
2. crates/server/src/handle/mod.rs:155-160: `with_session_created` sits under `set_wall_guard`'s doc comment.
3. run --help's --frame-budget line (crates/cli/src/verbs/flags.rs) says "a run's last frame is judged without the next"; only true for a run that stops at a vblank. A run stopped mid-frame (--to, breakpoint, interrupt) settles its last whole frame by the partial frame (reviewer probe probe_a_run_stopped_by_to_after_the_lcd_off_settles_the_busy_frame). help budgets is right.
4. The color_rom_on_dmg remedy wording lives only in crates/cli/src/render/created.rs; a serve or web client gets the bare enum. Move the remedy text beside SessionNote (protocol or bundle) so every client says the same, per the library-crate ruling.

criteria.label: each of the four is fixed

data.title: Loudness calls a 1-frame run silent, and its end-to-end test passes without the DAC gate (979993f)
data.description:
Found by review s15-r-views of 979993f. loudness_of (crates/audio/src/loudness.rs) always drops window 0; one frame is 547 samples = 1 window, so a 1-frame run measures nothing and the CLI prints rms_dbfs=silent for a channel that is sounding (loudness.gb after 30 frames: `run --frames 1 --audio-summary` -> take=square1 rms_dbfs=silent; it plays at -26.1 dB). Probe: s15rv_probe_tests.rs::probe_short_runs_report_square1_as_sounding (red).
Also: the end-to-end test the_summary_ranks_a_loud_channel_over_a_quiet_one_whose_dac_pops passes with DAC gating disabled (mutation: pass &[] instead of &switches[c]; all 15 audio_tests still pass), because loudness.asm's square 2 is on 6 frames, off 2, so clean windows outnumber pop windows. Make pop windows the majority (e.g. on 1, off 1) and assert the ungated figure differs.
Fix: tell "unmeasured" (no window left) apart from "silent", as a typed state on the wire, and state the minimum length in run --help.

criteria.label: a short run reports unmeasured, not silent (the probe, seen red)
the end-to-end loudness test fails with the DAC gate removed

data.title: help rgbds and the starter README misstate where INCLUDE looks; --audio-summary help imprecise (652bc56, 979993f)
data.description: Found by review s15-r-views of 652bc56. "include/ is the only folder INCLUDE searches by bare name" (help rgbds in crates/cli/src/help/topics.rs; the starter README crates/build/templates/README.md, pinned by the scaffold.rs test) is false: rgbasm runs with the project folder as its working directory (crates/build/src/project.rs:444 -> tool.rs:37 current_dir) and finds a bare INCLUDE there; the generated images folder is on the path when images exist (project.rs:212); --include DIR replaces include/ (layout.rs:68-80). True: src/ isn't searched. Suggested: "INCLUDE looks in the project folder and include/ (or --include), not beside the including file: src/ isn't searched". Also in run --help's --audio-summary line: windows are dropped within 128 samples of a DAC switch (GUARD), which can include a neighbor, not only "any in which a DAC switched"; and "loudest first" should say the mix comes first.

criteria.label: the include text is true, by test
the --audio-summary line names the guard and the mix-first order

data.title: shot accepts --screen-rows without --json, and its help claims more than the hash gives (3cd4e89)
data.description:
Found by review s15-r-views of 3cd4e89. `gbcli shot b.png --session a --screen-rows` (no --json) exits 0 and shows no rows (crates/cli/src/build/video.rs shot() sets screen: true; crates/cli/src/render/video.rs prints only pixels=), and the server still builds the 24-140 KB screen. Refuse it without --json (the house pattern for flags that would be ignored), on shot and run --shot.
Help nits in the same surface: the fingerprint's "a crop of another shape fingerprints differently" is false across kinds (a 6x1 DMG crop of shade 0, "000000", and a 1x1 GBC crop of black, "000000", collide; probe s15rv_probe_tests.rs::probe_shades_and_colors_of_one_byte_string_collide). The hash is Ben's ruling: narrow the claim to "among screens of one kind" in shot --help, ShotMade's doc and screen.rs (turn the probe into a test of the documented behavior). The --crop line still says "the 160x144 screen"; the SGB's frame is 256x224 with its border, kind colors, about 344 KB as rows, and help never mentions it.

criteria.label: --screen-rows without --json is refused, by test (seen red)
shot help, ShotMade doc and screen.rs say the fingerprint distinguishes shapes only within one kind, and the SGB size is named

data.text: s15-fix: fixed in worktree s15-r-views. Answer gains take_session_created() (default None); Handler and the CLI's Responder delegate. serve() puts the report on whatever response it writes first (parse error, non-UTF-8, panic) when that response has none; Handler::handle still attaches it for direct library callers, so the report is taken once wherever first. Batch goes through serve per line, so rows mode prints session_created before `line n=1`. No request lines: nothing on stdout, documented in gbcli schema's session_created line. Tests (serve.rs): bad line, non-UTF-8, panic (seen red), success once and empty input (green pins); CLI creation.rs batch rows + json + schema text (seen red by disabling the serve fill). The reviewer's frame-budget probes moved to handle/profile_tests.rs and engine tests/it/profile.rs (ROM renamed busy_wait_halt_off).

s15-fix: all four fixed in worktree s15-r-views. (1) render::rows and render::session_created each carry their own doc comment. (2) with_session_created's doc moved off set_wall_guard (and now says serve may give it on a response the handler never answered). (3) run --help --frame-budget: "a run that stops at a vblank, as --frames N does, judges its last frame without the next, so run one more to settle it" (run_help.txt golden re-blessed). (4) SessionNote::remedy(session) in gbcli-protocol (unit test seen red); the CLI's created.rs only renders it. Not carried on the wire: SessionNote is a bare enum string on the wire ("note": "color_rom_on_dmg", documented in gbcli schema), and putting a derived remedy beside it would mean a second field kept in step with the first; a Rust/web client calls note.remedy(name), a JSON client reads the note's meaning in gbcli schema.

s15-fix: fixed in worktree s15-r-views. Loudness.rms_dbfs is now gbcli_protocol::Level {Dbfs(Real), Silent, Unmeasured}: on the wire a number, "silent" or "unmeasured" (was number or null). Unmeasured = no window left after the first-window and DAC-guard skips (empty capture, a 1-frame run, or a switch beside every window); Silent = windows measured, none above the floor. CLI renders rms_dbfs=unmeasured (observe.txt golden step: run --frames 1 --audio-summary). run --help and gbcli schema state it, with the 1/32 s (two windows) minimum. Tests seen red: audio unit test a_capture_with_no_window_left_is_unmeasured_not_silent; server a_run_too_short_to_measure_reads_unmeasured_not_silent (red by mutating Unmeasured back to Silent). E2E: loudness.asm's square 2 is now on 2 frames, off 1 (was 6/2), so pop windows are the majority; with the reviewer's mutation (&[] for &switches[c]) the e2e test fails (square 2 reads -27.9, not -41.6); restored, it passes. Its sounding_s floor went 0.4 -> 0.15 (about one clean window a cycle, by design of the new ROM). On 1/off 1 was not used: switches every ~548 samples leave almost no clean window, so the gated figure would be unmeasured; on 2/off 2 dropped square 2's DC-inclusive WAV RMS under square 1's (2699 vs 2935), losing the trap. Optional done: FLOOR_RMS precomputed (8.23094945877059), pinned against FLOOR_DBFS by a test; log10 for the output figure remains.

s15-fix: fixed in worktree s15-r-views. build::video::shot refuses --screen-rows without --json ("--screen-rows only applies with --json" / "add --json to get screen.rows, or drop it"), so shot and run --shot both refuse (flag_tests seen red; the existing screen_rows test now passes --json; verbs.rows.txt golden now shows the refusal for its shot --screen-rows step, the json golden still shows rows). Fingerprint claim narrowed to "among screens of one kind" in shot --help, ShotMade::pixels doc and gbcli_view::fingerprint's doc; the reviewer's collision probe is now crates/view/src/screen.rs across_kinds_rows_of_the_same_bytes_share_a_fingerprint (pins the collision as documented). --crop names 160x144 / 256x224 on an SGB with its border; --screen-rows and shot --help name 344 KB on an SGB; a server test (shot_screen_tests on_color_models_the_rows_are_the_pngs_pixels) pins SGB 256x224 colors. Help text pinned by help.rs shot_help_narrows_the_fingerprint_claim_and_names_the_sgb_size (written after the text, so not seen red) and the run_help.txt golden.

s15-fix: fixed in worktree s15-r-views. help rgbds and the starter README now say "INCLUDE looks in the project folder and include/ (or --include), not beside the including file: src/ isn't searched." Tests: scaffold.rs README test and a new CLI help.rs test that help rgbds and the README (code marks stripped) carry the same sentence, both seen red; a new build test (crates/build/tests/it/build.rs a_bare_include_finds_the_project_folder_and_include_but_not_src) shows the text is true with the pinned RGBDS (green on first run: it confirms the reviewer's finding, no product change). The generated images folder, also on the path when images exist, is left unnamed per the suggested wording. run --help --audio-summary now says "the mix first, then the channels loudest first" and "any within 128 samples (1/256 s) of a DAC switching on or off" (pinned by observe.rs help test and run_help.txt; written with MWdKUC's unmeasured clause in the same line).
